agent_primer:
Adobe InDesign is the industry-standard page-layout app for print and digital publishing — books, magazines, brochures, posters, marketing collateral, and reflowable EPUB. Documents are spread-based; content lives inside **frames** (text frames, graphic frames, unassigned frames). InDesign has no command palette equivalent; canonical action surfaces are the top menu bar, keyboard shortcuts, the Tools panel (left edge), the Control panel (top, contextual to the active object), and a stack of dockable panels on the right. Most non-trivial operations open a modal dialog you must commit (Enter / OK) or cancel (Escape). The canvas and frame contents are largely opaque to the macOS accessibility tree — verification on InDesign should default to `interpret_check` (vision) for anything that affects layout, type, color, or graphics, and to `file_check` for anything that writes to disk (Package, Export PDF, Export EPUB, IDML).

Key UI elements (default Essentials workspace, latest InDesign):

- **Document window** (center): one or more spreads displayed vertically. Zoom level varies (`cmd+0` fit page in window, `cmd+alt+0` fit spread in window, `cmd+1` actual size, `cmd+2` 200%). Multiple open documents appear as tabs across the top of the canvas area; switch with `ctrl+tab` (yes — `ctrl`, not `cmd` — because `cmd+tab` is macOS app-switching). Pasteboard surrounds each spread; objects placed there are not printed but persist with the document.
- **Pages panel** (Window → Pages, `cmd+F12` on most layouts): the most-used panel. Lists every page in the document plus the **parent pages** (called **master pages** in versions before CC 2020 — InDesign 19+ uses "parent"). Drag-reorder pages, double-click to navigate, right-click for insert/duplicate/delete page actions. Parent pages live above a divider in the panel.
- **Layers panel** (Window → Layers, F7): document-level layers (NOT frame-level — InDesign frames are not Photoshop layers). Layers stack across all spreads. Visibility, lock, and print toggles per layer.
- **Links panel** (Window → Links, `cmd+shift+D`): tracks every placed asset (images, PDFs, .ai files, linked text). Assets are linked by default, not embedded. Modified linked files show a yellow warning triangle; missing files show a red stop sign. Use **Update Link** / **Relink** from this panel.
- **Character panel** (`cmd+T`) and **Paragraph panel** (`cmd+alt+T`): typography. The Control panel at the top of the screen mirrors most character/paragraph settings when a text frame or text selection is active. Character formatting: font family, font style, size, leading, tracking, kerning, baseline shift, all-caps/small-caps. Paragraph: alignment (left, right, center, justify, justify-last-left/right/center, full-justify), left/right indent, first-line indent, space before/after, drop caps, hyphenation, justification settings.
- **Paragraph Styles panel** (Window → Styles → Paragraph Styles, F11) and **Character Styles panel** (`shift+F11`): named style definitions. Apply with click; option-click redefines a style from current selection. Cmd-click skips local overrides on apply.
- **Swatches panel** (F5): named colors and gradients. CMYK, RGB, Lab, Spot, Tint, Mixed Ink. New Swatch from the panel menu opens the New Color Swatch dialog with a Color Type dropdown (Process / Spot) and Color Mode dropdown (CMYK / RGB / Lab / Pantone / etc.).
- **Stroke panel** (F10), **Color panel** (F6), **Gradient panel**, **Effects panel** (`cmd+shift+F10`).
- **Tools panel** (left edge): Selection tool (V, the black arrow — selects a frame as an object), Direct Selection tool (A, the white arrow — selects frame contents or anchor points), Page tool (`shift+P`, edit individual page sizes), Gap tool (U, adjust space between objects), Type tool (T, edit text inside a frame or create one by dragging), Type on a Path tool (`shift+T`), Line tool (`backslash`), Pen tool (P), Pencil tool (N), Rectangle Frame tool (F, graphic placeholder), Ellipse Frame tool, Polygon Frame tool, Rectangle tool (M, unassigned frame), Ellipse tool (L), Polygon tool, Scissors tool (C), Free Transform (E), Rotate (R), Scale (S), Shear (O), Eyedropper (I), Measure (K), Hand tool (H, pan), Zoom tool (Z), Apply Color / Gradient / None swatch swatches at the bottom.
- **Top menu bar**: `File`, `Edit`, `Layout`, `Type`, `Object`, `Table`, `View`, `Window`, `Help`. Menu paths are the most version-stable action surface; prefer them over raw keybinds when a keybind hasn't been verified on the user's specific InDesign version.
- **Control panel** (top, just under the menu bar): contextual. Selection tool active → frame X / Y / W / H / rotation / shear / scale / flip / fitting controls; Type tool active → character + paragraph settings, paragraph/character style dropdowns, find next style, eyedropper.
- **Story Editor** (`cmd+Y`): a separate text-only editor window for the current text thread. Useful for long-copy work; reflects back to the layout in real time.
- **Document tabs** (across top of canvas area): one InDesign window can host many open files.

Frame fundamentals:

- A **text frame** holds a text thread (one or more linked frames carrying continuous copy). Click the small out-port square at a frame's bottom-right to thread to another frame. **Smart Text Reflow** can auto-add pages when overset text exists.
- A **graphic frame** (the X-with-a-rectangle icon) holds a placed image or other linked asset. Use **File → Place** (`cmd+D`) to place into a selected frame — or click into empty space to drop an image at native size.
- An **unassigned frame** is a shape with stroke / fill but no content commitment.
- All frames support fitting options: **Object → Fitting** (Fit Content to Frame, Fit Frame to Content, Fit Content Proportionally, Fill Frame Proportionally, Center Content, Frame Fitting Options). Common shortcuts: `cmd+alt+E` Fit Content Proportionally, `cmd+alt+shift+E` Fill Frame Proportionally.

Undo / history:

- `cmd+Z` is single-step undo. `cmd+shift+Z` redoes / steps forward. InDesign keeps a long history during a session but does not persist it across saves.

Save / Export behavior — important and modal-heavy:

- `cmd+S` saves to the document's current path (always a `.indd`). On a new untitled document, this opens the **Save As** dialog instead.
- `cmd+shift+S` is **Save As**.
- `cmd+alt+S` is **Save a Copy** (writes a copy at a chosen path, leaves the in-memory document pointing at the original).
- **File → Export** (`cmd+E`) is the path for non-`.indd` outputs: PDF (Print), PDF (Interactive), EPUB (Reflowable), EPUB (Fixed Layout), JPG, PNG, IDML (InDesign Markup, the round-tripable XML format used for older-version compatibility), HTML, SVG. The Export dialog is a two-step flow: a Save dialog where you pick filename and choose Format from the dropdown, then a format-specific options dialog (e.g. PDF presets like "High Quality Print", "Press Quality", "PDF/X-1a:2001", "Smallest File Size").
- **File → Package** (`cmd+alt+shift+P`) collects the .indd, all linked assets, and all used fonts into a folder for handoff to a printer or another machine. Multi-step dialog: Summary → Fonts → Links and Images → Colors and Inks → Print Settings → External Plug-ins → Package button → second Save dialog for the package folder.
- **File → Preflight** (`cmd+alt+shift+F`) opens the Preflight panel and runs the active profile against the document.

Common modal dialogs to expect (the workflow's `pre_step` dismisses the most common transient ones with `escape`; user-initiated dialogs like Save As, New Document, Place, Export should NOT be escaped — they are part of intended flows):

- **Subscription / Update reminder** — transient overlay on launch. Safe to escape.
- **Welcome / Recent Files screen** — appears on launch with no document open. Safe to dismiss with escape, or click into a recent file or New.
- **Missing Fonts** — appears on file open if linked fonts aren't installed. Activates Adobe Fonts where possible; user-facing decision matters for production work but not for v0 layout-edit shortcuts.
- **Missing or Modified Links** — appears on file open. "Update Modified Links" / "Don't Fix" / "Fix Links Automatically".
- **Edit Original / Update / Relink** — confirmations on Links panel actions.
- **Save As file dialog** — user-initiated; do NOT escape.
- **Export file dialog** — two-step flow described above; do NOT escape.
- **New Document dialog** — appears on `cmd+N`; tabbed (Print / Web / Mobile) with size, orientation, pages, columns, margins, bleed/slug fields.

Accessibility-tree caveats:

- Frame contents (rendered text and placed graphics) are essentially invisible to the macOS AX tree. **Use vision (`interpret_check`) for any verification of layout state.**
- Modal dialog presence and button labels DO show up in the AX tree, but the v0 MCP doesn't expose them — interpret_check for modal verification too in v0.
- File-system writes verify cleanly via `file_check`.

Version notes: this seed targets InDesign 19+ (Creative Cloud 2024 / 2025 line, where the "master page" terminology was finalized as "parent page" in panel labels). Earlier versions (18 and below) may differ on: panel labeling (Master vs Parent), the default Export keyboard shortcut, and a handful of Object-menu fitting paths. If you're on an older version, prefer menu navigation over keybinds for save/export paths.
